system.name: Nebula
system.one_liner: a coherent acceleration framework for large-scale 3D Gaussian splatting collaborative rendering between cloud and VR client

components.name: Gaussians
components.role: the full set of scene Gaussians available for LoD search

components.name: Fully-Streaming LoD Tree Traversal
components.role: GPU-parallel full LoD tree traversal used for the initial frame

components.name: Cut Result
components.role: the appropriate-LoD set of Gaussians found for the current frame

components.name: Temporal-Aware LoD Search
components.role: reuses the previous frame's cut result to accelerate LoD search on subsequent frames

components.name: Management Table
components.role: tracks, per Gaussian, the reuse window since it was last in a cut result on the client

components.name: ΔCut Result
components.role: the Gaussians in the new cut that are not yet on the client

components.name: Compression
components.role: compresses the delta Gaussians before sending them to the client

components.name: Decompression
components.role: decompresses the delta Gaussians received from the cloud

components.name: Local Subgraph Update
components.role: merges the decompressed delta into the client's local Gaussian structure

components.name: Current Rendering Queue
components.role: the up-to-date set of Gaussians ready to be rendered

components.name: Sorting
components.role: sorts projected Gaussians for tile rendering

components.name: α-Check
components.role: checks accumulated opacity, shared by both eyes before the pipelines diverge

components.name: Color Blending
components.role: blends the final pixel color for the left eye's view

components.name: Stereo Reproj.
components.role: reprojects the shared alpha-check result to reconstruct the right eye's view without redoing full rendering

components.name: Merging & Filtering
components.role: merges and filters the reprojected result for the right eye

components.name: Right Eye
components.role: final rendered right-eye image, produced by reusing most of the left eye's computation

flows.what: initial full LoD tree traversal (orange path)
appropriate-LoD cut of Gaussians for the initial frame
previous frame's cut reused for temporal coherence
newly encountered Gaussians not yet on the client

alpha-checked contribution for the left eye
shared intermediate result reused for the right eye
merged and filtered contribution for the right eye

content.key_idea: Nebula offloads memory-intensive LoD search to the cloud, which streams only newly needed compressed Gaussians to the client; the client renders both eyes together, reprojecting one eye's result to avoid redundant work.
content.reading_order: Left to right and top-down within each dashed region: Cloud's LoD search feeds the Management Table and Compression, crossing into Client's Decompression, queue, then the two-eye pipeline.

evidence: Fig. 9 shows the overall workflow of our pipeline.
Nebula offloads the memory-intensive LoD search to the cloud while the client side executes the remaining operations
Our system in the cloud maintains a management table that tracks the set of Gaussians currently stored on the client

summary: This figure gives an end-to-end overview of Nebula's workflow, split into a Cloud side and a Client side by a vertical divider, with a top legend distinguishing three arrow types: initial-frame LoD search (orange), subsequent-frame LoD search (green), and remaining client rendering (gray). On the cloud, Gaussians undergo a full streaming LoD tree traversal for the first frame or a temporal-aware LoD search that reuses the previous cut for later frames; a management table tracks which Gaussians the client already has, so only the delta (ΔCut Result) is compressed and sent. The client decompresses this delta, updates its local subgraph, and queues Gaussians for rendering through Projection, Sorting, and an α-Check; the result is blended for the Left Eye while also being reprojected and merged to cheaply produce the Right Eye's view, avoiding duplicate rendering work.
